title: Shantideva: Calling for Help
speaker: Nomon Tim Burnett
summary: Nomon Tim Burnett tells the legend of Shantideva, the monk at Nalanda nicknamed Busuku for eating, sleeping, and pooping, who recited the Bodhicharyavatara from a teaching seat built to embarrass him and then floated out a window. Nomon reads from chapter two, "Confession of Faults," where Shantideva admits harm done and calls for help to Samantabhadra, Manjushri, Avalokiteshvara, and Jizo. Nomon then describes a restless night when a vision of teaching in the Zendo came to mind and calmed body and mind into sleep. Chapter three turns back to light with the prayer "May I be medicine for the sick," and Nomon closes on its last line about inexhaustible delusions and the question of how to end them.
